newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian driving rules offend humanity - EU's Kinnock.
newsitem.headline: Belgian driving rules offend humanity - EU's Kinnock.

text.p: EU Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock ridiculed Belgium's priority-to-the-right driving rules on Wednesday, pouring scorn on a regime that regularly causes bent fenders and bemuses tourists.
"There are no words I could use with a mixed audience on a family show about this way of getting thrills in an otherwise boring life," Kinnock told a news conference on EU road safety.

"I consider it quite frankly to be an offence to the security and liberty of the human race," he added about the system which gives vehicles absolute priority over those arriving from their left unless otherwise indicated.
While Belgium is not alone in Europe in applying priority to the right, its drivers enforce it with sometimes suicidal gusto, often when they do not actually have the right of way.

European Commission figures put Belgium seventh among EU countries in the table of people killed per million cars registered, with 366 people killed in 1994 compared with Portugal's 1,043 and Sweden's 164.
